To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the value of equity is a sum of two parts.

the equity value can be decomposed into two components, the no-growth and the growth value; the no-growth value is proxied by the capitalised next period’s earnings, or the open-book value; and the growth value is a function of the market risk, retention rate, and return on earnings retained.
the value of equity is equal to the value of the no-growth component and the value of the growth component.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the valuation of equity in an environment where the term structure of interest rates and future cash streams are both stochastic.
the valuation of equity in a stochastic term-structure framework.

the determination of value in a stochastic term structures of interest rates framework and it has shown that the value of equity has two components, one is a no-growth or stable growth component and another is growth component.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the value of equity is the sum of the value of the existing business (no-growth component) and the value of the growth component, which in turn depends on the risk adjusted return on investment opportunities.
the value of a firm is the sum of the present value of the no growth value and the present value of future growth.
the value of equity is determined by a no-growth and growth components and the growth value is a function of retention rates and the persistence of returns on equity retained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the value of equity is determined by the risk-adjusted future growth of earnings and the risk-adjusted value of the no-growth component.

in the presence of stochastic term structure of interest rates, the value of a firm is determined by the growth rate in earnings performance, the persistence in returns on retained earnings, the market risk and the retention rate.

the equity value is a function of growth rates and risk-adjusted future earnings, the latter being the product of the growth in book value and the risk adjusted return on equity, and the former being the product of retention rate, persistence of returns on retained earnings and the market systematic risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth value is an explicit function of the market risk and the risk premium, which is consistent with the asset pricing theory and the market risk is a function of the systematic market risk.
the value of equity is not only dependent on the risk adjusted return on investment but also on the risk-adjusted growth rate of investment and the risk-adjusted return on investment.
in the absence of growth, the value of equity is equal to the capitalised next period's earnings.
